name: Zurishaddai
title: Father of Shelumiel, leader of the tribe of Simeon
summary: Zurishaddai is known from the books of Moses as the father of Shelumiel, who was the leader of the tribe of Simeon during the wilderness wanderings. He is mentioned in connection with the census and the organization of Israel's camp at Sinai. Although little is known about his personal life, his family played an important role in the tribal divisions of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Shelumiel appointed as tribe leader
keyEvents.description: Zurishaddai's son Shelumiel was appointed leader of the tribe of Simeon and represented the tribe in the organization of the people of Israel.

keyEvents.title: The tribe of Simeon in the camp
keyEvents.description: Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai, received his place in the camp arrangement on the south side of the tabernacle together with the camp of Reuben.

keyEvents.title: The census at Sinai
keyEvents.description: Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai, helped count the fighting men of the tribe of Simeon, which numbered 59,300 men.

keyEvents.title: Dedication offering from the tribe of Simeon
keyEvents.description: Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai, presented his offering at the dedication of the altar as a representative of the tribe of Simeon.

keyEvents.title: Commander of the Army of Simeon
keyEvents.description: Selumiel, son of Shedeur, was placed in charge of the army of the tribe of Simeon during Israel's departure from Sinai.
